correctness.rationale: The source confirms unique W^{2,1} invariant densities for each theta. A rank-two inverse-branch BV inequality 3 lambda² Var+16 lambda² L1 gives uniform bounded variation near 2; dyadic quadrature then proves interior uniform and global L1 convergence. Exact weight rescaling gives G; a uniformly contracting inverse recursion gives H, uniformly on compact s. Endpoint transfer derivatives give exact slopes and their limits; trace inequalities prove no W1 convergence and W2 blowup. The finite-grid program independently checks algebra and two scaled profiles; no finite computation is used to establish the continuum limit.

value.rationale: The motivating work proves unexpectedly high fixed-parameter W^{2,1} regularity at a critical cusp exponent; its degeneration as cusp strength vanishes is a natural, unaddressed statistical stability question. The theorem resolves it at two different boundary scales with exact profiles, reveals a dyadic preimage cascade at the fixed endpoint, and distinguishes L1 statistical stability from Sobolev failure via sharp endpoint constants. These are nontrivial invariants of the concrete family rather than routine reformulations.
